S. 1, Special Branch Station. File No.................... Date December 14, 1941

SUBJECT: Chapei Police request municipal Police escort to prisoners passing the Settlement from Chapei to Nantao

On December 13, a telephone message was received by the undersigned from Mr. Ohashi, Japanese advisor to the Chapei Police, stating that owing to shortage of gasoline, the use of motor cars for sending prisoners from Chapei to Nantao, will be ceased, and that the following arrangement has been decided upon :-

On every Tuesday and Friday, the prisoners under the Chapei Police escort will leave the Garden Bridge at 11 a.m. and proceed on foot along The Bund to Nantao via French Concession. At each time, there will be from 6 to 14 prisoners with an escort of 2 to 6 Chapei Police Constables. These constables are unarmed.

(楊天送) age 20, married, Room 103, H. No. 33 Sze-
native of Canton. taken by me D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung ching Rd.
at C.B.H.Q. (C.1) on the 29.7.38 and translated by Clark Hsu.

I am employed as an assistant in the opium shop, conducted
by one named Yang Hai Cheng alias Yang Siau K, which is located
at Room 103, House No. 33 Sze-ching Road.

On 1.7.38 I came to Shanghai from Swatow and on 7.7.38,
I encountered in the vicinity of "Dah Woo" Hotel, F.C. one of
my old friends, named Lieu S Yah, who then introduced me to
work with the opium shop, owned by Yang Siau K. with pay at
$10.00 per mensem. Out of one oz. of opium sold, I received
10-cents as transaction fee.

At 11 a.m. 8.7.38 I noticed a man, native of Northern
province, came to my place of employment and take out from his
waist 2 packets of opium which he handed over to a female
deliverer. She in turn, gave the opium to Yang Siau K, who
then concealed same beneath a bed. I further observed the
cloth bag, containing the opium, bear Chinese characters
"Tientsin". From this I learned that the opium came from
Tientsin.

Opium was being retailed at the above address in various
quantities.

At about 2 p.m. on 11th July, a telephone call was received
at this opium shop, which call was answered by Yang Siau K him-
self, who, on putting back the receiver, appeared to be very
frightened. He immediately removed out the opium from beneath
the bed and then had same wrapped in paper. On completion of
packing up the opium he left the premises without informing
anybody of his destination.

Several minutes afterwards the premises were raided by

REPORT

Subject ILL-TREATMENT OF PRISONER BY THE JAPANESE GENDARMES.

Made by D.S.I. MAKLAEVSKY Forwarded by D.I. GLOVER

Sir,

I beg to report that at 12.10 p.m. July 17th. 1938
Yoon Ping Chien ( 赵秉谦 ) 1st. arrested person, was returned
to C.B.H.Q. (C.I) by Sergeant - Major K-toda of the Japanese
Gendarmerie. The man complained of having been beaten, whilst
in the custody of the Japanese Gendarmerie and as he bore
unquestionable marks of ill - treatment, he was immediately sent
to the Police Hospital. He was examined by Dr. Knuk who issued
a certificate reading as follows:-

" Multiple bruises of the back and limbs,
evidence that the prisoner had been
severely flogged in the last 2 or 3 days."

His condition was not found serious and he was not
detained at the Hospital.

The man stated that he was subjected to a severe
flogging on several occasions when he was being questioned by
Japanese Gendarmes with regard to counterfeit Japanese Military
